Test Case: Audit every DID in the fleet and the faucet pair before the run: the total held, locks, stuck tokens, double ownership, counters, chain history
Expected Result: Total held equals the 400000 RBT the faucet minted; nothing locked or stuck; every token owned by one DID; counters match the real tokens
Also Check In Same Run: Free, pledged, committed and burnt-for-FT split; nodes whose database could not be read

Test Case: Senders on different machines all transfer at once through one quorum, rung by rung: 10, 20, 50, 70, 90, 100, 150, 200, 220 - first 1 RBT each, then the ladder again with one fractional amount, which makes the quorum split its own tokens for every pledge
Quorum Setup: one quorum signs for every sender
Expected Result: Record the largest number of concurrent transfers one quorum signs in full, whole and fractional (saved for the later cases)
Also Check In Same Run: p50 / p95 / max time and refusal reasons per rung; senders refused for their own tokens counted apart; database check on every sender and the quorum
Code Ref: core/quorum_initiator.go:17 QuorumRequired=1; core/consensus/consensus.go:18 quorum pledges exactly the value

Test Case: Build a big wallet of thousands of whole tokens from the faucet, and a fragmented wallet from change sent by 30 wallets at once, round after round
Expected Result: Both wallets reach their size; record what it cost
Also Check In Same Run: Faucet speed per token; part tokens collected per round; 30 concurrent transfers into one wallet
Code Ref: core/parts/denom.go split tree; core/wallet GetSplitAndNonsplitTokenDenom uses existing parts first

Test Case: Send 1, 100 and 1000 RBT from the big wallet, then ten 50 RBT transfers from it at once, then fractional amounts paid in part tokens from the fragmented wallet
Expected Result: Every amount the wallet can cover goes through and is credited
Also Check In Same Run: Time per amount; refusals from the known second-hand part-token bug are tagged

Test Case: Every owner at once mints two FT series (one at the 1000-per-RBT cap) and re-mints the first under the same name; each series passes through 6 wallets; each owner sends to 5 wallets at once; two series move in one transaction
Expected Result: Every holder of every series shows exactly what it should
Also Check In Same Run: Mint and transfer times; the re-mint (numbered on from 1000) adds to the count instead of making a second series

Test Case: Every owner at once creates and deploys 2 NFTs, mints 3 children under the first, executes it, has a subscriber on another node execute it, and passes the second NFT through 6 owners
Expected Result: Children listed under their parent; the chain is equal on the owner and the subscriber; each NFT shows with its last owner only
Also Check In Same Run: Time per operation; how long a subscriber's and a new owner's node take to hold the NFT (each acts only once it does)

Test Case: Contracts from every owner at once; 4 subscribers per contract join at depths 1, 3, 4 and 6 while the owner and two subscribers keep executing
Expected Result: Every subscriber's chain matches the owner's on every contract
Also Check In Same Run: Deploy, execute and subscribe times; how long each executor's copy of the chain takes to catch up (each executes only once it has); which contracts diverge and on which node

Test Case: Audit every DID in the fleet and the faucet pair after the run and compare with AUDIT-START
Expected Result: Total unchanged since the start; nothing locked or stuck; every token owned by one DID; no new counter drift
Also Check In Same Run: Committed and burnt-for-FT growth since the start; counter drift carried over from earlier runs

Test Case: Pay an amount just below, at, and just above each quorum's own free holding, to find the exact boundary of what one quorum can pledge
Quorum Setup: five quorums, each probed at its own holding
Expected Result: The largest transfer a quorum signs equals its free holding; one RBT more is refused for insufficient quorum liquidity
Also Check In Same Run: boundary matches the holding to within a token; refusals above it name quorum liquidity, not the sender
Code Ref: core/consensus/checks.go:539 pledge >= value; core/transaction.go:253 insufficient quorum liquidity

Test Case: A quorum that has pledged tokens for one transfer then spends its own free RBT in another transfer
Quorum Setup: the sender is itself a quorum, self-wired
Expected Result: The quorum's free send goes through and the tokens it pledged are left untouched
Also Check In Same Run: the pledged token_ids are unchanged after the free send; value conserved across the three DIDs
Code Ref: core/callback.go:14 pledge held until spent onward; core/wallet/pledge.go:486

Test Case: A quorum whose tokens are all pledged tries to spend; then, once the pledge is released, it spends a whole token it pledged and a fractional amount of one
Quorum Setup: the sender is itself a quorum, self-wired
Expected Result: Record what the ex-quorum DID can spend: a whole-token spend of a released pledge is refused (known bug), a fractional split of it goes through
Also Check In Same Run: pledge release is timed; the refusal names the ex-quorum bug; the split send is credited
Code Ref: core/consensus/checks.go:308 ex-quorum spend bug; split bypasses via new part token

Test Case: A wallet holding a single token fires the same 1 RBT to many receivers at the same instant - only one may win
Expected Result: Exactly one of the concurrent sends is accepted and the rest refused - no double spend
Also Check In Same Run: the winner is credited; the token is never Free under two DIDs
Code Ref: core/wallet/token_lock.go token lock; core/consensus/checks.go double-spend guard

Test Case: Many DIDs on one node, then on one machine, all transfer at once through one quorum - the node and the machine under full concurrent load

Test Case: One RBT passed along a long chain of wallets, a different quorum validating each hop, beside a control chain of the same depth signed by one quorum
